title: Cardiac rehabilitation
what: An exercise program supervised by a doctor and instructor, to help your heart recover after illness or surgery. It includes exercise and advice on diet and lifestyle.
why: After a heart attack, a stent, bypass or valve surgery, or with heart failure, when your doctor says it is safe.
duration: a session usually lasts 45 to 60 minutes; the program usually runs several weeks. Your doctor will decide
tell_doctor: Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or irregular heartbeat in recent days
If you feel dizzy or faint
If your joints or back hurt. Exercises will be adapted

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before starting, you usually have an ECG, sometimes a stress test and heart ultrasound. This helps set a safe level of exercise.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them as usual. Do not stop them on your own. If you have questions, tell your doctor, and they will decide.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light meal 1 to 2 hours before. Do not exercise on an empty stomach or right after a big meal.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Sportswear, comfortable shoes, and a bottle of water.

bring: Your hospital discharge papers and latest ECGs
Pills your doctor told you to keep on hand
steps: Before the session, your blood pressure and pulse are checked
Sometimes a heart monitor is attached
Warm-up: easy walking and light movements
Main part: exercise bike, treadmill, or exercises at your own pace
The load is increased gradually from session to session
At the end, a cool-down and another blood pressure and pulse check
feel: The effort feels moderate: you can talk, but singing is hard
Mild muscle tiredness after the first sessions
after: Your doctor will give you a plan for home exercise and walking
Keep a diary of your pulse, blood pressure, and how you feel
Regular exercise matters more than hard exercise
red_flags: Chest pain or pressure that does not go away at rest: stop and call emergency services
Severe shortness of breath, fainting, or sudden dizziness: tell the instructor right away

faq.q: Is it dangerous to exercise after a heart attack?
faq.a: Not under a doctor's supervision. The load is set from your tests and increased gradually.

faq.q: Can I exercise at home instead of a center?
faq.a: Part of the program is often done at home. Your doctor will decide what level suits you.

reminders.text: Cardiac rehab session tomorrow. Light breakfast, medicines as usual. Bring sportswear and water.
